newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann sees profit rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann sees profit rise in 1997.

text.p: German engineering and telecoms group Mannesmann AG said on Friday it expected a further improvement in operating profits this year after a 10 percent gain in 1996.
In a regulatory news release, the company said its D2 mobile phone business would grow but that would be offset by startup costs in new telecoms areas, particularly at the Mannesmann Arcor venture.
Mannesmann Arcor is a joint venture with state railways Deutsche Bahn AG in which Mannesmann owns 49.8 percent.
Mannesmann last month said it had made a group profit in 1996 of one billion marks on ordinary activities, up from 911 million marks.
Mannesmann shares came under heavy pressure on Friday as dealers said that a respected investment research house had downgraded the stock.
Mannesmann shares were down 17 marks at 635 in the final hour of bourse trading in Frankfurt, but sharply above a session low of 617 marks.
The company also said its engineering and tubes and trading divisions would show "noticeable improvements" this year, while its automotive section would post a modest improvement.
